Hi Elaine — thanks for the note and the sample CSV, that’s helpful. Looping in Neha (account lead) and Karthik (billing/engineering) so we can give a concise breakdown.

High level answers up front:
- We aggregate token usage by active conversation window (session) before applying the billing quantum, not by individual API call. That reduces overcount for apps that stream or do many small calls within a continuing context.
- Long-history windows (32k) are billed as the active context length at the time of generation. We apply prefix/KV caching credits when the server detects repeated reuse of prior context; cached KV usage won’t be recounted each call.

Karthik — can you confirm the rounding rule that produced the 2–3% deviation and whether anything in BrightCart’s CSV looks like an edge case (heartbeat messages, multiple short streams that should have been merged)?

Hi all,

Thanks for the sample — I pulled the CSV and ran it against our metering engine. Short answer: the ~2.8% variance is consistent with expected behavior given BrightCart’s distribution of very short streaming calls interleaved with long-history generations. Details below (will also put this into the 1‑pager).

How we count (summary):
1) Session aggregation first: for any conversation/session id we merge sequential calls with <=120s gap into a single active-window bucket.
2) Tokenization and quantum: we tokenize the merged prompt+response and apply the billing quantum of 8 subtokens (our metering quantum) per line item. We round up the session total to the nearest quantum.
3) KV cache crediting: when a token range is served from cache (prefix reuse), we apply a negative adjustment (credit) at invoice time; this is visible as a separate line item.
4) Streaming: streaming frames inside a single session are treated as intra-session fragments and are aggregated before rounding. However, short isolated one-off streams that never reattach to the same session will be charged as separate sessions (this is the biggest source of variance).

Specifics for the CSV rows you highlighted:
- Call id X-9812: two short streams (frames 00 and 01) were not stitched into the same session because there was a 4.5 minute gap; they therefore rounded separately. If you can identify this pattern we can reclassify them as a single session for the billing reconciliation.
- Call id X-9827: long-history generation (32k) — large portion served from prefix cache, so invoice shows both full token count and a positive cache-credit recovery line ~ -14 tokens.

Suggested immediate steps:
- We can provide a per-session mapping CSV with the rounded quantum applied and an explanation column. That will let your controller see exactly where rounding happened.
- For recurring small streams that you expect to be stitched, we can tighten the session gap threshold for BrightCart’s tenancy (configurable) — that will reduce rounding overhead.

I’ll attach a short example mapping in the next message.
